page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 24 dedicated physical cores with one thread per core, totaling 24 vCPUs. It features 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor, includes a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps, and does not feature local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance dichotomy between single-core and multi-core workloads. Single-core performance is a notable bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the weak and poor categories respectively. Single-threaded gzip compression also registers in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by average-tier results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth remains consistently average across both small cached and large uncached read/write operations.

Given the 192.0 GB memory capacity and average multi-core processing capabilities, this instance is configured for memory-intensive workloads that do not rely heavily on single-thread speed. Appropriate workloads include database operations, Redis caching layers, and medium-scale text or image processing. The lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, which should be factored into the overall resource architecture. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a dense memory profile relative to its CPU allocation, making it suitable for memory-bound applications that can tolerate moderate CPU performance.
